items.name: NullableInterval
items.summary: An [Interval] that also tracks null status using a boolean interval.

methods.name: and
methods.signature: fn and<T: Borrow<Self>>(&self, rhs: T) -> Result<Self>
methods.summary: Returns an interval representing the set of possible values after applying SQL three-valued logical AND on each combination of possible values from `self` and `other`.

methods.name: apply_operator
methods.summary: Apply the given operator to this interval and the given interval.

methods.name: contains
methods.signature: fn contains<T: Borrow<Self>>(&self, other: T) -> Result<Self>
methods.summary: Decide if this interval is a superset of, overlaps with, or disjoint with `other` by returning `[true, true]`, `[false, true]` or `[false, false]` respectively.

methods.name: contains_value
methods.signature: fn contains_value<T: Borrow<ScalarValue>>(&self, value: T) -> Result<bool>
methods.summary: Determines if this interval contains a [`ScalarValue`] or not.

methods.name: data_type
methods.summary: Get the data type

methods.name: from
methods.summary: Create an interval that represents a single value.

methods.name: is_certainly_false
methods.summary: Return true if the value is definitely false (and not null).

methods.name: is_certainly_true
methods.summary: Return true if the value is definitely true (and not null).

methods.name: is_certainly_unknown
methods.summary: Return true if the value is definitely null (and not true or false).

methods.name: is_false
methods.summary: Returns the set of possible values after applying the `is false` test on all values in this set. The resulting set can only contain 'TRUE' and/or 'FALSE', never 'UNKNOWN'.

methods.name: is_true
methods.summary: Returns the set of possible values after applying the `is true` test on all values in this set. The resulting set can only contain 'TRUE' and/or 'FALSE', never 'UNKNOWN'.

methods.name: is_unknown
methods.summary: Returns the set of possible values after applying the `is unknown` test on all values in this set. The resulting set can only contain 'TRUE' and/or 'FALSE', never 'UNKNOWN'.

methods.name: not
methods.summary: Returns an interval representing the set of possible values after applying SQL three-valued logical NOT on possible value in this interval.

methods.name: or
methods.signature: fn or<T: Borrow<Self>>(&self, rhs: T) -> Result<Self>
methods.summary: Returns an interval representing the set of possible values after applying SQL three-valued logical OR on each combination of possible values from `self` and `other`.

methods.name: single_value
methods.summary: If the interval has collapsed to a single value, return that value. Otherwise, returns `None`.

methods.name: values
methods.summary: Get the values interval, or None if this interval is definitely null.

items.name: apply_operator
items.summary: Applies the given binary operator the `lhs` and `rhs` arguments.

items.name: cardinality_ratio
items.summary: This function computes the selectivity of an operation by computing the cardinality ratio of the given input/output intervals. If this can not be calculated for some reason, it returns `1.0` meaning fully selective (no filtering).

items.name: satisfy_greater
items.signature: fn satisfy_greater(left: &Interval, right: &Interval, strict: bool) -> datafusion_common::Result<Option<(Interval, Interval)>>
items.summary: This function updates the given intervals by enforcing (i.e. propagating) the inequality `left > right` (or the `left >= right` inequality, if `strict` is `true`).

items.name: Interval
items.summary: The `Interval` type represents a closed interval used for computing reliable bounds for mathematical expressions.

methods.name: and
methods.signature: fn and<T: Borrow<Self>>(&self, other: T) -> Result<Self>
methods.summary: Compute the logical conjunction of this (boolean) interval with the given boolean interval.

methods.name: arithmetic_negate
methods.summary: Reflects an [`Interval`] around the point zero.

methods.name: cardinality

methods.name: cast_to
methods.summary: Casts this interval to `data_type` using `cast_options`.

methods.name: contains
methods.signature: fn contains<T: Borrow<Self>>(&self, other: T) -> Result<Self>
methods.summary: Decide if this interval is a superset of, overlaps with, or disjoint with `other` by returning `[true, true]`, `[false, true]` or `[false, false]` respectively.

methods.name: contains_value
methods.signature: fn contains_value<T: Borrow<ScalarValue>>(&self, other: T) -> Result<bool>
methods.summary: Decide if this interval contains a [`ScalarValue`] (`other`) by returning `true` or `false`.

methods.name: data_type
methods.summary: This function returns the data type of this interval.

methods.name: equal
methods.signature: fn equal<T: Borrow<Self>>(&self, other: T) -> Result<Self>
methods.summary: Decide if this interval is certainly equal to, possibly equal to, or can't be equal to `other` by returning `[true, true]`, `[false, true]` or `[false, false]` respectively.

methods.name: gt
methods.signature: fn gt<T: Borrow<Self>>(&self, other: T) -> Result<Self>
methods.summary: Decide if this interval is certainly greater than, possibly greater than, or can't be greater than `other` by returning `[true, true]`, `[false, true]` or `[false, false]` respectively.

methods.name: gt_eq
methods.signature: fn gt_eq<T: Borrow<Self>>(&self, other: T) -> Result<Self>
methods.summary: Decide if this interval is certainly greater than or equal to, possibly greater than or equal to, or can't be greater than or equal to `other` by returning `[true, true]`, `[false, true]` or `[false, false]` respectively.

methods.name: intersect
methods.signature: fn intersect<T: Borrow<Self>>(&self, other: T) -> Result<Option<Self>>
methods.summary: Compute the intersection of this interval with the given interval. If the intersection is empty, return `None`.

methods.name: into_bounds
methods.summary: Converts this `Interval` into its boundary scalar values. It's useful when you need to work with the individual bounds directly.

methods.name: is_superset
methods.signature: fn is_superset(&self, other: &Interval, strict: bool) -> Result<bool>
methods.summary: Decide if this interval is a superset of `other`. If argument `strict` is `true`, only returns `true` if this interval is a strict superset.

methods.name: is_unbounded
methods.summary: Checks if the interval is unbounded (on either side).

methods.name: lower
methods.summary: Returns a reference to the lower bound.

methods.name: lt
methods.signature: fn lt<T: Borrow<Self>>(&self, other: T) -> Result<Self>
methods.summary: Decide if this interval is certainly less than, possibly less than, or can't be less than `other` by returning `[true, true]`, `[false, true]` or `[false, false]` respectively.

methods.name: lt_eq
methods.signature: fn lt_eq<T: Borrow<Self>>(&self, other: T) -> Result<Self>
methods.summary: Decide if this interval is certainly less than or equal to, possibly less than or equal to, or can't be less than or equal to `other` by returning `[true, true]`, `[false, true]` or `[false, false]` respectively.

methods.summary: Convenience function to create a new `Interval` from the given (optional) bounds, for use in tests only. Absence of either endpoint indicates unboundedness on that side. See [`Interval::try_new`] for more information.

methods.summary: Create an interval from -π to π.

methods.name: make_symmetric_unit_interval
methods.summary: Creates an interval between -1 to 1.

methods.name: make_unbounded
methods.summary: Creates an unbounded interval from both sides if the datatype supported.

methods.name: make_zero
methods.summary: Creates a singleton zero interval if the datatype supported.
